summary: Iteration 10: Verified 4 security fixes (SEC-001 CORS, SEC-002 webhook signing, SEC-003 SSRF guard, SEC-005 Node internal auth) plus regression coverage on auth/sessions/v2/docs. 21/21 pytest tests pass.

minor.issue: The Cloudflare/K8s ingress in front of the preview URL injects its own permissive 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' header on OPTIONS responses, effectively overriding the backend's SEC-001 fix from a browser's perspective. Direct hit to http://localhost:8001 confirms the FastAPI middleware is correct (rejects evil origins, echoes the allowlist origin with credentials=true). This is an infrastructure/edge concern, not a backend code bug — but until the ingress is reconfigured, the practical CORS posture on the public URL remains permissive.

The SSRF url_guard check runs AFTER the 'no connected session' check. In practice this is not exploitable (attacker still cannot reach the fetch without a connected WhatsApp session) but it makes the guard invisible in HTTP tests when no session is connected. Consider moving check_url() call above _resolve_session() so the guard is authoritative regardless of session state (defence in depth). Unit tests on url_guard.check_url directly confirm the guard logic itself is correct.

action_items: (Optional) Reorder url_guard.check_url() to run BEFORE session resolution in /api/v1/messages and /api/v2/sendMessage so the SSRF guard is provably enforced in end-to-end HTTP tests.
(Optional / infra) Configure the Cloudflare/K8s ingress to stop injecting 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' so the backend's strict CORS allowlist becomes user-visible.
critical_code_review_comments: SEC-001 CORS middleware (server.py:1687-1706) is correctly implemented: refuses wildcard+credentials, defaults to localhost only when unset, allow_credentials properly gated. Verified at uvicorn directly.

SEC-002 webhook handlers (billing.py:441/542/697) correctly return 503 when signing secret / PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID missing. Stripe additionally 400s earlier when STRIPE_SECRET_KEY empty — both paths refuse unsigned traffic; no billing state change possible.

SEC-003 url_guard.py denies loopback, RFC1918, link-local (169.254/16 incl. AWS metadata), CGNAT (100.64/10), IPv6 ULA/link-local, plus non-http schemes. Redirect hops are re-checked (max 5). Applied at 3 known call-sites (server.py:1422 & second location, v2_compat.py:303 & 700).

SEC-005 wa-service/server.js:361-380 uses crypto.timingSafeEqual with length check to prevent length-leak; /health stays public; backend wa_client.py forwards the header. Direct localhost:3001 verified: 401 without header, 401 with wrong header, non-401 with correct header, 200 on /health.
Minor ordering concern: SSRF guard runs after session resolution in v1/messages and v2/sendMessage — see minor issue above.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing seeded admin + sessions.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 4 security fixes verified in /app/backend/tests/test_security_fixes.py. Two observations were reported to main agent (non-blocking): (a) Cloudflare edge overrides CORS on the public URL — backend itself is correct; (b) SSRF guard runs after session-connected check, so on preview (no connected session) it's masked behind the earlier 400. Unit tests on url_guard.check_url prove the guard logic is correct. All regression tests (health, admin login+cookies, sessions list, v2 grouplist, v2 account with session key, sendMessageFile validation, /developer public, /api/messages) pass.
